problem:
Solve for $x$ in $Ax=b$ given that the matrix $A$ is orthogonal, and 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} & -\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} & 0 \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{5} \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

feedback.problem: Find the inverse of the orthogonal matrix $D=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} & -\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}].$
feedback.worked_solution:
The inverse of an orthogonal matrix is equal to its transpose.

Therefore, since $D$ is orthogonal, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}^{-1} & ={D}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} & -\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
